description: One source copied many times: wire stories republished verbatim or with attribution, an official release reposted, a single social-media post relayed by several outlets, one unnamed report repeated. However many articles there are, it is one source, so the answer is NO_EFFECT. Some copies are caught by the deterministic family rules; others (paraphrased relays, attributions the rules do not recognize) need the classifier to see that the outlets are not independent.

cases.summary: A wire exclusive republished verbatim by three aggregators.

items.title: Exclusive: US prosecutors prepare charges against crypto exchange Zanthor, sources say
Exclusive: US prosecutors prepare charges against crypto exchange Zanthor, sources say
Exclusive: US prosecutors prepare charges against crypto exchange Zanthor, sources say
Exclusive: US prosecutors prepare charges against crypto exchange Zanthor, sources say

cases.why: One wire exclusive based on anonymous sources, syndicated verbatim: one source.

cases.summary: Two crypto sites rewrite a wire exclusive and credit the wire.

items.title: Exclusive: Crypto exchange Paxora under US sanctions probe, sources say
Paxora faces US sanctions probe, Reuters reports
Report: US investigating exchange Paxora over sanctions, per Reuters

cases.why: The rewrites attribute the wire: copies of one source.

cases.summary: Two small sites relay an AP report, crediting 'the Associated Press'.

items.title: Hackers hit crypto exchange Velmont, freezing customer withdrawals
Exchange Velmont freezes withdrawals after hack, the Associated Press reports
Velmont hack: withdrawals frozen, according to the Associated Press

cases.why: One AP report and two attributed relays. The deterministic rules recognise the credit 'the Associated Press' in any capitalisation, so the three articles are one family whatever the classifier lists (before R4d they matched it only in lower case and counted three).

cases.summary: Three outlets relay one post on X by an exchange CEO.

items.title: Kryvex CEO says on X that withdrawals will be limited for a few days
Kryvex boss warns of withdrawal limits in post on X
Kryvex to cap withdrawals, CEO tweets

cases.why: Articles quoting one social-media post are not independent of that post.

cases.summary: Three small sites paraphrase one late-night message from an exchange founder.

items.title: Exchange founder hints at withdrawal limits in late-night message
Founder of exchange Nexabit warns users may face withdrawal caps
Nexabit withdrawal caps coming? Founder's remarks spark concern

cases.why: All three relay one message; the wording avoids the phrases the rules look for, so only the classifier can collapse them to one source.

cases.summary: A wire headline reposted unchanged by two aggregators.

items.title: Cleveland Fed president says another rate increase cannot be ruled out
Cleveland Fed president says another rate increase cannot be ruled out
Cleveland Fed president says another rate increase cannot be ruled out

cases.why: One remark, one source; the aggregators add nothing. It is also hedged, not a decision.

cases.summary: A lender's own press release distributed through a newswire.

items.title: Halcyon Lending Announces Temporary Pause of Customer Withdrawals
Halcyon Lending Announces Temporary Pause of Customer Withdrawals
Halcyon Lending Announces Temporary Pause of Customer Withdrawals

cases.why: One company statement distributed verbatim: one source, with a calm market.

cases.summary: The same rumor headline with only case and punctuation changed.

items.title: BREAKING: SEC to sue crypto exchange Lumora
Breaking - SEC to sue crypto exchange Lumora!
breaking: sec to sue crypto exchange lumora

cases.why: Identical headlines once case and punctuation are normalized: one copied claim, about a future lawsuit, with no named source.

cases.summary: Three small sites repeat one unnamed report with different wording.

items.title: Report: SEC preparing lawsuit against exchange Lumora
SEC preparing lawsuit against exchange Lumora - report
Lumora reportedly faces SEC lawsuit

cases.why: All three cite the same unnamed report; the headlines differ, so the rules count three families and the classifier must collapse them.

cases.summary: Two regional sites relay one Korean media report.

items.title: Korean exchange Hanbit halts deposits after abnormal withdrawals, local media report
Hanbit suspends deposits, citing abnormal outflows, Korean media say

cases.why: Both relay the same local media report; neither reported it independently.

cases.summary: An SEC release and two verbatim reposts of its headline.

items.title: SEC Charges Crypto Lender Brightvault With Defrauding Retail Investors
items.excerpt: The Securities and Exchange Commission today charged Brightvault Capital and two executives with misleading investors about the safety of customer deposits.

items.title: SEC Charges Crypto Lender Brightvault With Defrauding Retail Investors
SEC Charges Crypto Lender Brightvault With Defrauding Retail Investors

cases.why: An official release alone is still one source until independent reporting or the market confirms it; verbatim reposts add nothing (calm market).

cases.summary: Three sites relay one Bloomberg scoop.

items.title: Bloomberg: Exchange Torvane weighs suspending US customers
Torvane may suspend US users, Bloomberg reports
Torvane considering a US exit, according to Bloomberg

cases.why: Every article relays one Bloomberg report, and the report is about a possibility, not an action.
